summary: NEW (Round 2 only): when a Book call is retried against an already-consumed offer token, the resulting HTTP 409 'This booking has already been created' error response includes the full raw supplier SOAP request AND response verbatim in OriginalSupplierRequest/OriginalSupplierResponse — including the travel agency's plaintext apiKey and secretKey used to authenticate to the GulfAir/TPConnects backend. This leak is unconditional: the triggering Search call had isDebug=false, yet the downstream Book error still carried the raw supplier payloads.
spec_ref: SPEC.md §7.14 (supplierRequest/supplierResponse credential-leak guardrail, previously documented only for isdebug=true on Search)
expected_value: OriginalSupplierRequest/OriginalSupplierResponse omitted or redacted on error responses, regardless of the isDebug flag on the originating request
impact: Any caller who retries a Book call (e.g. after a client-side timeout, a common and realistic scenario — see the accompanying latency finding) receives the live supplier agent's apiKey/secretKey in plaintext in the HTTP response body. This is a credential-leak vector distinct from and more serious than the already-documented isdebug=true Search-only leak, since it fires on an ordinary error path with no debug flag involved.
